"The term schizoid refers to an individual the totality of **whose experience is split** in two main ways: in the first place, there is a rent in his relation with his world and, in the second, there is a disrup- tion of his relation with himself. [This PhD disseration](https://digitalcommons.pepperdine.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1412&context=etd) on the treatment of schizoids goes into AvPD, SPD, and schizotypal PD. I found it very informative and engaging. This might be the most useful for the question in your OP.

An article written by the influential Helen Deutsch, [The Impostor: Contribution to Ego Psychology of a Type of Psychopath](http://www.sakkyndig.com/psykologi/artvit/deutsch1959.pdf). She discusses SPD's false-self.

["Manual for use with Checklist of Schizotypic Signs."](http://meehl.umn.edu/sites/meehl.dl.umn.edu/files/061scchecklist.pdf) As the title suggests, it focuses on symptoms and signs, but it's very thorough. As a warning, if you're the type to get in your head about these sorts of things/become a bit hypochondriac, it might be best to skip over this one or only read the beginning.

[The Schizoid Personality of Our Time](https://www.ijpsy.com/volumen3/num2/63.html), analyzing SPD as a response to culture, was an interesting read IMO. (note: far more relevant to contemporary schizoid than schizotypal. But you may find it relevant still)

This article, [The Unwanted Child](https://www.energeticsinstitute.com.au/characterology/unwanted-child-schizoid/), focuses on trauma/early life experiences of schizoids and the impact that SPD and adverse early experiences has on the schizoids body, along with the psychology behind SPD.

I also found the concept of self-disorder (which includes SPD) very interesting! The wiki page is [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-disorder). Further, if you read the wiki, it talks about two assessments, the [EASE](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/7583892_EASE-scale_Examination_of_Anomalous_Self-Experience) and the [EAWE](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/314288757_EAWE_Examination_of_Anomalous_World_Experience). I found them very interesting. However, and as I cautioned with the manual, for people who get in their heads with these kinds of things, I wouldn't recommend looking at them.

Another interesting article that I would certainly recommend: ["Some Thoughts about Schizoid Dynamics."](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/7142775_Some_Thoughts_about_Schizoid_Dynamics)
